stage_a.note: The founders maintain a warm, engaged demeanor while describing the problem, using upbeat delivery.
Strong engagement with the product solution, showing genuine excitement about how it works.
Friendly and approachable interaction, especially when bringing out their daughters to demonstrate the problem.

venture.description: A disposable hair catcher that fits into shower and bathtub drains to prevent clogs.
venture.note: The founders are asking for $300,000 in exchange for 5% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves and state their ask of $300,000 for 5% equity in their company.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark reacts to the high valuation with surprise.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond reacts to the high valuation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara reacts to the high valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders state they have a problem and introduce their five daughters.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that the father is in trouble with five daughters.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders explain that the problem is the daughters' hair, calling them professional drain cloggers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin reacts to the image of the clogged hair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders describe how cleaning the shower drain is a disgusting job nobody wants to do.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark laughs at the presentation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders demonstrate how the product catches hair and can be easily disposed of after months.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara reacts with disgust to the visual of the caught hair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders explain the product's design features and invite the daughters to hand out samples.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark jokes about what the founder did in a previous life to have five daughters.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: The founder jokes back that having five daughters was destiny.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The daughters distribute samples of the product to the investors.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks the founders how they came up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer explains the invention was an accident discovered when her husband pulled dental floss and hair out of the drain.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara reacts to the story of the invention.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer adds that they realized they could make a product out of solving their own problem.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks about the manufacturing cost and the selling price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer states that the double pack costs about $1.20 to make.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks what the double pack retails for.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford replies that the double pack sells for $9.99.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin notes that the profit margins are excellent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks where the product is currently available for purchase.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer lists major retailers where it is sold, including Walmart and Bed Bath & Beyond.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond acknowledges that they have achieved widespread retail distribution.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks the founders to provide their sales numbers.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford reveals they have sold $14.2 million in retail.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark expresses amazement at the high sales figure.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin reacts with surprise to the sales numbers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond notes that the sales figure is very large.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks if the product was sold through an infomercial.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer confirms that it was sold via infomercial.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks why they need an investment if they are already everywhere and doing great.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer explains they didn't know the industry and were contacted by an infomercial company after a trade show.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they entered into a deal with the infomercial company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer confirms they did a deal and were eventually passed to the largest infomercial company in America.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if they have been in the agreement for three years.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford states they have received $800,000 in royalty payments.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori clarifies if that amount was in aggregate over the three years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks if it is a three-year license deal with the company.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford clarifies that they are currently in the third year of the deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks if and when the deal runs out.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford explains they gave them five years, ending in March, but renegotiating would end it immediately.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks if anyone else currently holds equity in the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer confirms that they own everything.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks for clarification about a previous angel investor.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford explains they paid back the angel investor using the royalty payments, so they are out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin recaps their sales and royalties, concluding they are here to get a partner to take back control.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer agrees with Kevin's assessment of their situation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori sympathizes, noting that they are simply trapped in a bad deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer elaborates on the frustration of seeing their product in stores but losing most of the money to middlemen.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford states their goal is to form a company, take the product to market, and keep the profits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond challenges them on wanting the investment to build out a full company infrastructure from scratch.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that their motivation is to take control of their product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer confirms Kevin's summary of their motivation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks how they plan to execute on building the company and notes they need the investors' resources.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer admits they need the investors' help and resources to execute.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark exits because he doesn't want to invest and then have to reinvent their entire business for them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin offers $300k for 20%, stating he needs more equity for the headaches of renegotiating their contracts.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori exits, explaining she understands their frustration but believes they can keep doing it on their own.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond matches Kevin's offer of $300k for 20%, noting he likes the product but needs more than 5%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara makes an offer of $300k for 25%.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond points out to the founders that Barbara's offer asks for more equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara defends her higher equity ask, arguing that retail and infomercials are her sweet spot.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford counters the sharks, asking if anyone would do the deal at $300k for 10%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara questions the 10% counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer argues that the sharks are treating it like an unproven new product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond pushes back, reminding them that the sharks have already given their offers.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Gifford counters again, offering 15% for the $300k.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond immediately rejects the 15% counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer pitches a new angle, pointing out that clogged drains are a major complaint in hotels.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond admits that he likes the idea of targeting the hotel industry.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin likes the hotel concept and agrees to revise his offer to accept the 15%.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks Kevin to confirm if he is doing the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jennifer enthusiastically accepts Kevin's revised offer.

decisions.note: He does not want to invest and then have to reinvent their business for them.
He needs more equity to deal with the headaches of renegotiating their contracts.
She believes they can keep doing it on their own and keep their equity.
He likes the product but 5% is not enough equity for him.
She asks for more equity because retail and infomercials are her sweet spot.
They believe the product is proven and shouldn't be treated like a new item.
They offer slightly more equity after their 10% counter is met with skepticism.
He accepts the 15% counter-offer because he likes the concept of targeting hotels.
